reason: This passage emphasizes strict hierarchy throughout. It depicts clear chains of command: Ahab reports to Jezebel (v. 1-2), God issues direct commands to Elijah about anointing new leaders (v. 15-16), and Elisha immediately becomes Elijah's servant in obedience, leaving his livelihood to follow (v. 21). The text stresses divine authority, prophetic succession ('prophet in your place'), master-servant relationships, and God's sovereignty over a remnant people. The passage reinforces rather than discourages institutional hierarchy and obedience to established authority.
